Who wrote the Bible? Probably this guy, because he claims to be the best and that his family will rule the world according to God's will. Eventually, David has a son named Solomon, considered one of the two best rulers of Israel along with David, marking what we call the Davidic kingdom.

But after Solomon, the Israelites turned wicked again. God punished them by scattering Israel across the world. The last covenant is the arrival of Jesus, who reasserted the law of Moses and sacrificed himself to free humanity from original sin—eating the fruit—which was the first disobedience against God. By killing himself, Jesus redeems humanity, and everyone can now be with God without following specific laws or being part of David's family.

This creates Christianity. The first five covenants are what Jews believe. They still expect someone to restore the kingdom of David but not Jesus. Christians believe Jesus is the final prophet and that he is actually God himself. This leads to Christianity, the belief in Jesus Christ.

The major issues with this understanding include why God banished humans from the Garden of Eden after eating fruit, which seems strange given human nature. Also, why did God destroy the world through Noah if it was still wicked afterward? And why did Jesus have to sacrifice himself?

According to esoteric beliefs, God destroyed the world because of Nephilim, not humans. For more insight, read "The Book of Enoch" and "The Gospel of Thomas."
